notes: In person now means in person. Emojis are gone from in-person scenes — the mode is narrative prose, and a smiley mid-narration breaks it — cut mechanically from the stream and the finished reply (the same policy stripActions applies to texting in the other direction, because asking a model politely never fully settles it when the history is full of texting turns to copy), and the system prompt says so too. Pictures in an in-person scene changed meaning entirely: there is no phone and nobody is sending anything — the picture paints what YOU see with your own eyes at that moment, the character seen from the outside from where you stand. The character no longer acknowledges a picture request in their prose; the scene just keeps moving, and the image shows the view. The photo director gets an in-person briefing — stage the user's own view, camera at their eye position, the character never holding a phone, no cameras or mirrors that aren't in the scene — while texting chats keep the selfie machinery exactly as it was: framing, references, the works, because there the character really is sending you a picture.
